title: Buttermilk Biscuits
description: Tall, flaky buttermilk biscuits made with cold butter and a quick fold, ready in about 35 minutes from start to finish.
scaleNote: A double batch fits on one large baking sheet if the biscuits just touch; bake times stay the same.
equipment: {len 2 1/2 in} round cutter or a sharp knife

image.alt: A pan of tall golden buttermilk biscuits

ingredients.prep: spooned and leveled, plus more for the counter

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 450F oven} with a rack in the upper-middle position. Line the baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Scatter in the cold butter and pinch it into the flour with your fingertips until the largest pieces are the size of peas.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Some dry bits at the bottom are fine.

Tip the dough onto a floured counter and pat it into a rectangle about {len 1 in} thick. Fold it in thirds like a letter, pat it out again and repeat the fold twice more. The folds make the flaky layers.
Pat the dough {len 1 in} thick and cut straight down with the cutter, without twisting. Set the biscuits on the sheet so they just touch. Press the scraps together once and cut the rest.
Brush the tops with a little buttermilk and bake until tall and deep golden on top, {time 15-18 min}. Brush with melted butter as they come out, if you like.

notes: Keep everything cold. If the butter softens while you work, chill the cut biscuits for {time 10 min notimer} before baking.
No buttermilk? Stir {qty 1 tbsp} lemon juice into {qty 1 cup} milk and let it stand for 5 minutes.
Biscuits are best warm. Freeze unbaked biscuits on a tray, then bag them; bake from frozen, adding a few minutes.
